**Meta description:** Compare Cheers Cash alternatives for Shopify on price and payout, from store credit and points to insured cashback paid by Venmo or PayPal.


## Introduction


Shopify brands looking at Cheers Cash alternatives usually want the same thing. A promotion that gives shoppers money back without eating the margin.


The options sort neatly once you ask two questions. How does the shopper get paid, and whose budget carries the payout?


This is Playably's own blog, so read it with that in mind.[Playably](https://playably.ai/) runs one of the five options below, the insured event-triggered rebate, and we say plainly where the other four fit.


You won't find rival prices or payout rates here. Each app lists its own plan on the Shopify App Store, so check the listing for the current number.


What this piece compares is structure. What the shopper receives, where it can be spent, and who pays for it.


If you want the head-to-head first, start with[our Playably vs Cheers Cash comparison](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/playably-vs-cheers-cash-2026-cash-rebates-the-platform-pays-for-vs-4-000-a-month-gift-card-rebates) .


### Key Takeaways


- Cheers Cash alternatives split on who funds the payout and how shoppers get paid.
- Store credit and points keep the reward inside your store, funded by your margin.
- With Playably, the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps full margin.
- Playably pays shoppers 100% back by Venmo or PayPal when the trigger hits.
- Compare the payout cost, not only the plan fee.


## What to Compare in a Cheers Cash Alternative


Four questions sort the five options in this list.


- **How is the shopper paid?** Cash, store credit, a gift card or points.
- **Who funds the payout?** Your margin, your discount budget, or someone else.
- **What does the brand pay?** A plan fee, a share of sales, a build fee, or a mix.
- **What shows at checkout?** Full price, or a lowered one.


The last question matters more than it looks. A reward earned after a full-price checkout leaves your advertised price alone.


A lower checkout price is a fair tool too. It just moves the cost onto the price itself.


The margin math behind that choice is in[cash back vs discount codes](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/cash-back-vs-discount-codes) .


## The 5 Alternatives at a Glance


Alternative How the shopper is paid Who carries the payout What the brand pays


1. Store credit cashback apps A balance to spend in your store Your store, as product handed over on a later order The app's listed plan, plus the credit when redeemed


2. Gift card rebate apps A gift card Depends on the app's model The app's listed plan, plus whatever its model charges


3. Loyalty points apps Points toward a later reward Your store, when points are redeemed The app's listed plan, plus redeemed rewards


4. Gamified reward apps A reward the game unlocks, such as a discount or a perk Your store, when the reward is a discount The app's listed plan


5. Insured event-triggered cashback (Playably) 100% of the order back by Venmo or PayPal, if the trigger hits Playably insures and hedges the payout $0 of the rebate, with performance pricing


Plan fees are easy to line up. The payout column is where the real cost sits.


Playably's triggers, and the moments behind them, are published on[the upcoming offers page](https://playably.ai/pages/upcoming-offers) .


## 1. Store Credit Cashback Apps


Store credit cashback returns part of an order as a balance the shopper spends back in your store.


It works as a repeat-purchase nudge. The shopper has a reason to return, and the reward stays inside your catalogue.


The cost is real, though. Store credit is product you hand over on the next order, so it comes out of margin when it gets redeemed.


**Good fit:** brands whose main goal is a second order, and who are comfortable funding the reward themselves.


If your list already waits for the next deal before buying, read[how discount fatigue sets in](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/discount-fatigue) before adding another reward layer.


## 2. Gift Card Rebate Apps


A gift card rebate pays the shopper back with a gift card instead of cash or credit.


Depending on the app, that card may be for your store or for another retailer. Who funds the card, and when, also varies by app.


Read the listing and the terms closely. Ask who pays the card's value, when that cost lands, and what happens if the shopper never redeems it.


**Good fit:** brands that want a reward with a gift feel and are happy to work through the app's terms.


If you're weighing a gift card against cash in hand, the team can show you the difference when you[book a Playably demo](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) .


## 3. Loyalty Points Apps


Points programs reward each purchase with a balance that converts into a discount, a product or a perk later.


They suit brands with frequent repeat buyers. A growing balance gives a regular shopper a reason to stay.


The payout is deferred, not removed. When points convert, the reward still comes out of your store's margin.


Points also pay back slowly. A balance that builds over several orders gives a first-time shopper less to act on today.


**Good fit:** brands with a loyal base and a long repeat cycle. For the playbook, see[gamification for loyalty programs](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamification-strategies-for-loyalty-programs-keeping-customers-coming-back) .


## 4. Gamified Reward Apps


Gamified apps put a short game in front of the shopper, such as a swipe, a product matchup or a quiz, and unlock a reward at the end.


The game is the hook. The reward is usually a discount or a perk, and your store funds it.


Playably has an app in this slot too.[The PlayAbly app](https://apps.shopify.com/playably) is listed on the Shopify App Store as free, with swipe-to-shop and product matchup formats, email capture and a real time dashboard.


Setup needs no coding.


A discount at the end of a game is a fair choice for plenty of promotions. It lowers the price the shopper pays, so the prize and your margin come from the same place.


**Good fit:** brands that want engagement and email capture first. For the wider shelf, see[our gamification app ranking](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/playably-best-gamification-app-2026) .


## 5. Insured Event-Triggered Cashback (Playably)


Playably runs a gamified conditional rebate tied to a real world trigger event.


Shoppers buy at full price and get auto-entered, with no code to remember. If the trigger hits, Playably pays them 100% of their order back by Venmo or PayPal, usually within days.


The payout is the difference. Playably insures and hedges the payout, so the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps its full margin.


Playably carries the payout, so your store never books the liability. Your exposure is a small, fixed amount agreed in advance.


Triggers come from a library of pre-modelled moments across sports, weather and culture, with new moments added weekly. You can also bring your own.


The results hold up. Jordan Craig's NFL Draft rebate posted "+34% bigger baskets than the store average, at full price", and "93% of buyers walked past two 25%-off sitewide sales running the same month."


The detail is in[the Jordan Craig case study](https://playably.ai/pages/jordancraig-case-study) .


BlackBoxMyCar recorded 18.25× ROAS on rebate ads during March Madness 2026.


**Good fit:** Shopify brands that want a headline offer at full price, without funding the payout.


## What Playably Costs


Playably prices rebate campaigns on performance. You only pay when a sale happens, and Playably carries all the risk.


No rate is published for the rebate campaign itself. Playably frames the cost as coming from your discount budget, money you'd give away anyway.


Two builds sit alongside the campaign:


- [**The Tier 1 build fee](https://playably.ai/products/tier-1-build-fee) .** About $1,500 one time for a gamified email and landing page test with a quiz and a dedicated brand strategist, plus a 15% revenue share on transactions from shoppers who played the game or gave their email during play.
- [**The bespoke shoppable game build](https://playably.ai/products/build-fee-bespoke-shoppable-game-build) .** Estimated at $10K to $25K, based on the complexity of the game concept, custom illustrations and development requirements. You own the game and the data it generates.


Playably publishes no minimum revenue, no minimum order volume and no contract length. Anything beyond that comes out of the demo call.


## How to Choose Between Them


Start with the job you need the promotion to do.


- **A second order?** Store credit or points.
- **A gift feel?** A gift card rebate, once you've read the terms.
- **Engagement and email capture?** A gamified reward app.
- **A headline offer at full price, with the payout off your books?** An insured event-triggered rebate.


Then run the margin check. Ask each option who pays the reward, and when.


Keep the data whichever way you go. In a Playably campaign, each play returns zero party data that feeds segmentation, recommendations and lifecycle flows long after the campaign ends.


More on that in[zero party data collection](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/zero-party-data-collection) .


## Conclusion


Cheers Cash alternatives come in five shapes. Store credit, gift cards, points, gamified rewards and insured event-triggered cashback.


The first four pay the reward as credit, a card, points or a perk, on the store's terms or the app's. The fifth hands the payout to Playably.


If your goal is a full-price offer that pays shoppers real money back, Playably's gamified rebate lets the brand pay $0 of the rebate. Your team approves the brief, and Playably runs every one.
